25.explanation: The FM opened the 2026-27 Budget 'on the sacred occasion of Magh Purnima and the birth anniversary of Guru Ravidas' (1 February 2026).

26.explanation: The FM credited the government's choices for favouring 'action over ambivalence, reform over rhetoric, and people over populism'.

sources.title: YourStory: FM Nirmala Sitharaman presents Budget 2026

27.explanation: The Budget describes India sustaining high growth of around 7% with moderate inflation.

sources.title: News on AIR: Union Budget 2026-27 leads towards vision of developed India

28.explanation: The Budget announced support for three dedicated chemical parks on a cluster-based, plug-and-play model.

29.explanation: The fiscal deficit falls from about 6.4–6.5% of GDP in 2022-23 to 4.3% (BE 2026-27), a drop of about 2.1–2.2 percentage points.

sources.title: Swarajya: Key takeaways from Union Budget 2026-27

29.note: 2022-23 figure (6.4% vs 6.5%) determines whether the decline is 2.1 or 2.2 pp; check Budget at a Glance.

30.explanation: Among the options, Defence has the largest allocation in the 'Expenditure of Major Items' table, ahead of transport, rural development and home affairs.

sources.title: Union Budget 2026-27: Budget at a Glance – Expenditure of Major Items

31.explanation: PESA makes the Gram Sabha's consultation or consent necessary before land acquisition and lets it prevent alienation of tribal land, making it a gatekeeper rather than an advisory or revenue body.

32.explanation: PESA puts the Gram Sabha at the centre of self-governance in Scheduled Areas.

33.explanation: PESA covers the ten Fifth Schedule States: Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan and Telangana.

34.explanation: Gram Sabhas got ownership of minor forest produce and control over local resources, turning forest dwellers from wage earners into economic stakeholders.

35.explanation: Common reform suggestions are to harmonise PESA with the Forest Rights Act, the Samata judgment (1997) and MGNREGA, which all concern tribal land, resources and livelihoods.
35.note: Opinion-type question; passage does not specify the laws.

36.explanation: The colonial Indian Forest Act, 1927 consolidated State control over forests and curtailed tribal customary rights.
36.note: The 1865 Act was also British; options (a) and (b) both fit the wording.

37.explanation: The passage says a crisis would test 'global norms governing nuclear restraint and security guarantees', which points to the NPT regime.

38.explanation: Canada shares maritime boundaries with Greenland (Nares Strait, Lincoln Sea, Hans Island) and overlapping Arctic continental-shelf claims, so it would have to deal with the US instead of Denmark.
38.note: Denmark itself would lose its Greenland-based Arctic claims, so (d) is arguable.

39.explanation: Greenland is central to monitoring the GIUK (Greenland–Iceland–UK) gap, the chokepoint for North Atlantic access.

40.explanation: Greenland is a self-governing autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.

41.explanation: The US presence (e.g. Pituffik Space Base) is governed by the 1951 Defense of Greenland Agreement with Denmark.

42.explanation: The European Central Bank runs monetary policy for the euro area.

43.explanation: Bulgaria borders Romania, Serbia, North Macedonia, Greece and Türkiye. It does not border Albania.

44.explanation: Bulgaria's currency before the euro was the lev.

45.explanation: The Maastricht Treaty (1992) created Economic and Monetary Union and the basis for the euro.

46.explanation: Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026, becoming the 21st euro-area member.

47.explanation: Türkiye is a NATO member but not in the EU. Greece, Spain and Croatia are in both.

48.explanation: The main legal concern was unpaid US assessed contributions. The 1948 joint resolution on US WHO membership conditions withdrawal on one year's notice and full payment of dues.

sources.title: Wikipedia: United States withdrawal from the World Health Organization

49.explanation: The WHO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

50.explanation: Smallpox was declared eradicated in 1980 after the WHO-led campaign.

51.explanation: World Health Day, 7 April, marks the WHO's founding in 1948.

52.explanation: President Trump initiated the withdrawal by executive order on 20 January 2025, and it took effect in January 2026.

sources.title: Wikipedia: United States withdrawal from the World Health Organization
